## 2. Export Format & Message Structure

### Format Specification
All three files originate from an **iOS WhatsApp export client** with 24-hour time formatting:
```text
[dd/mm/yy, hh:mm:ss] Sender Name: Message content
```
- **Date / Time Delimiters**: Enclosed in square brackets `[...]`, 2-digit day/month/year, comma separator, 24-hour time with seconds (`hh:mm:ss`).
- **Sender Delimiter**: Colon and single space `: ` after the closing square bracket.
- **Multi-line Messages**: Text lines that do not begin with `[dd/mm/` represent continuation lines of the preceding message. The parser buffers lines until the next bracketed timestamp.
- **Media Placeholders**: Attachments are referenced inline via `<attached: filename.ext>` (e.g. `<attached: 00000001-PHOTO-2025-10-31-15-28-56.jpg>`).
- **System Messages**: Lines without a sender string after the bracketed timestamp represent system actions:
  - *Group creations / title changes*: `[28/10/25, 21:04:12] Messages and calls are end-to-end encrypted...`
  - *Member joins / removals*: `[19/06/26, 14:12:00] +91 XXXXX XXXXX joined using this group's invite link`
- **Deleted Messages**: Explicit placeholder strings: `This message was deleted` or `You deleted this message`.

## 3. Review Morphology & Text Patterns

Student reviews in the chat archives do not follow a rigid form schema. Instead, they manifest in five primary structural patterns:

### Pattern 1: Multi-Candidate Inquiry
Students post short comparative queries requesting opinions on alternative professors for a specific subject:
> *"Who is a better teacher in jahangeer siddiq , Radha r , Dinakaran for java marks wise and teaching wise"*  
> *"any reviews for (Pugazhenthi R CSE103) (Sivakami R CSE104) and (Gomathi D MAT207)"*

### Pattern 2: Behavioral & Grading Commentary
Free-text qualitative descriptions describing grading severity, temper, attendance tolerance, or quiz policies:
> *"He generally has a bad temper and doesn't give marks easily."*  
> *"Ez marks and friendly"*  
> *"devi yamani means strictly follow her method other slot methods means getting mark difficulty"*  
> *"the only thing im concerned about is if hes petty in giving internal marks nd lab"*  
> *"Did she teach well or just give marks?"*

### Pattern 3: Slot Swapping & Trade Requests
Transactional messages during active FFCS registration attempting to trade slots:
> *"Operating System (E1+TE1) Have: Rajalakshmi ( L43+L44) Want: Thomas Abraham (L33+L34)"*

### Pattern 4: Hinglish & Colloquial Slang
Heavy use of campus jargon and Hinglish abbreviations:
- `chill` (lenient / low stress)
- `ez` (easy)
- `profs` / `mam` / `sir`
- `CATs` / `FATs` (Continuous Assessment Tests / Final Assessment Tests)
- `DA` (Digital Assignment)
- `blacklisted` (strictly avoided by students)

### Pattern 5: Numeric Score Snippets
Direct rating mentions embedded in prose:
> *"Prof X is solid 9/10 for internal marks, but 6/10 for teaching"*

## 5. Privacy, PII & Safety Guardrails (Rule 8 Compliance)

The raw chat archives contain sensitive personal data:
- **Phone Numbers**: 100+ unique raw international/Indian telephone numbers (`+91 XXXXXXXXXX`) appearing in sender strings and join logs.
- **Personal Names**: Real student first/last names.
- **Student ID Numbers**: Occasional registration numbers (e.g. `25BCE...`) shared in messages.

### Sanitization & Ingestion Policy
1. **Never reproduce raw phone numbers or real student identities in application databases or UI**.
2. **Regex Anonymization Pipeline**:
   ```python
   # Scrub phone numbers
   text = re.sub(r'\+?\d{1,4}?[-.\s]?\(?\d{1,4}?\)?[-.\s]?\d{3,5}[-.\s]?\d{3,5}', '[PHONE_REDACTED]', text)
   # Hash sender to synthetic UUID
   sender_id = hashlib.sha256(raw_sender.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:12]
   ```
3. **Review Extraction Only**: When extracting faculty feedback, only the extracted review excerpt and the matched faculty ID are retained in the database; sender metadata is dropped completely.
